subject: how much of the wider world is touched (§11.17 ruling)
canon: lore only for v1, matching the notes' own header distinction (whole world vs. game map, wb §9). It seeds the codex's world-map page (unreadable-scripts and traveller's-tale entries, mechanics.md row 33) and gives off-map merchants/pilgrims/diviners something real to reference (sea_caravan_docks already brings Gulf trade in). No playable off-map venture is built to it until the map itself grows past the City of the Moon (per D-002's 'grow city-by-city only if it works') — future scope, not v1 scope
source_ref: D-018; wb §9; notes L144-151; respects game-design §10's scope-reality warning

subject: the player's homeland (§11.5 ruling — the name, people and culture)
canon: the Land of Kaldun, the Kaldunai people — a marsh-and-lowland nation south of the two great rivers, conquered by the Empire two generations before the game's present (fits 'conquered long ago', notes L3). Chaldean-like per the notes' own word: reed-built villages amid marsh and levee, herding and fishing beside grain; a plain, undecorated Aramaic-adjacent tongue (distinct from Sumerian/Akkadian — gives the player a starting-language slot that isn't the setting's own); no state cult of their own survived the conquest, only household ancestor-reverence carried in exile — which is why the player reads city-life's dead-customs so readily. The Kaldunai never appear on the v1 map (game-design §11.2: homeland stays lore-only, reinforcing the exile) — they exist through the player's own memory, a handful of Kaldunai names in the diaspora quarter of the City of the Moon, and nothing else
source_ref: D-018; game-design §3;§11.5; notes L3 ('a chaldean like nation or state that got conquered by a great empire long ago'); grounded loosely in the real Chaldean marshland/Aramaic profile without claiming to BE Chaldea (the notes say 'like', not '=')
